children: Projects include new aluminium casting and alloy wheel facilities, a Bengaluru moulding expansion and a Maharashtra plant with Toyoda Gosei

Auto components manufacturer Uno Minda on Tuesday announced a series of capacity expansion and plant consolidation projects across its key business verticals, involving a combined investment of around Rs 1,415 crore.

The projects include a new aluminium casting facility in Hosur, a two-wheeler alloy wheel plant in Kharkhoda, expansion of a moulding facility in Bengaluru and a new plant in Maharashtra through its joint venture with Toyoda Gosei, Japan.
Uno Minda said the investments are aimed at increasing manufacturing capacity and meeting demand from original equipment manufacturers (OEMs).

The company will invest Rs 510 crore to establish a greenfield aluminium casting facility at Hosur, Tamil Nadu. The facility will manufacture casting parts for two-wheelers, four-wheelers and commercial vehicles, covering both internal combustion engine (ICE) and electric vehicle (EV) applications.

The new facility will be developed on an existing land parcel at Thally Road, Hosur, as the company’s current facility at the location has reached its practical expansion limits. The project will increase aluminium casting capacity at Hosur from around 13,000 MT to 34,000 MT at peak capacity.
The expansion will be implemented in phases over the next three years, with the first phase expected to commence production by Q4FY28.

The company’s board has also approved a 3.3 million-unit two-wheeler alloy wheel plant at Kharkhoda, Haryana. The project involves relocating two million units of existing capacity from Supa, Maharashtra, to Kharkhoda and an additional investment of Rs 155 crore. The first phase is expected to commence production by Q4FY28, with the project to be implemented over two years.

Uno Minda’s board has further approved an expansion of its moulding facility in Bengaluru, operated through subsidiary Uno Minda Kyoraku. The expansion, involving an estimated capex of Rs 80 crore, is expected to commence operations by Q1FY28.

Separately, Toyoda Gosei South India, the company’s joint venture with Toyoda Gosei, Japan, will establish a new plant at CSN, Maharashtra, with an estimated investment of Rs 670 crore. The facility will manufacture interior and exterior automotive parts, airbags, hoses and body sealing parts.

The Maharashtra facility will be Toyoda Gosei South India’s third plant in India, following facilities at Bidadi and Harohalli in Karnataka. The project is backed by new customer orders and is expected to commence operations by Q4FY29.
